items.title: CPLP: Angola, Cabo Verde and Timor-Leste stand out in IMF growth forecasts, Mozambique to recover gradually
items.summary: According to IMF data for Sub-Saharan Africa, Angola is expected to grow by 4.4% in 2026, up from the 3.1% estimated for 2025, before slowing to 3.3% in 2027. Inflation is, however, expected to remain high, albeit on a downward trajectory, falling from 20.2% this year to 10.6% in 2026 and 10.2% in 2027 The Cabo Verde archipelago will remain among the best-performing Portuguese-speaking African economies, with growth of 5% in both 2026 and 2027, following an estimated expansion of 6.3% in 2025 Inflation is expected to remain under control, at 1.2% this year and 2.8% in 2027. The IMF also forecasts a stable unemployment rate of 8.5% over the three years analysed In Guinea-Bissau, economic growth is expected to slow slightly from 5.8% in 2025 to 4.7% in 2026, before recovering to 4.9% in 2027. Inflation is expected to range between 2.1% and 2.5%, whilst the current account deficit is expected to remain high, fluctuating between 5.7% and 7% of GDP Mozambique, meanwhile, is expected to see a gradual recovery following an estimated contraction of 0.2% in 2025.

items.title: Iran: Political infighting deepens as economic woes mount during war
items.summary: Hardliners are stepping up pressure on Iran's government and calling for Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's removal. The oil minister resigned, but that's doing little to ease the pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian Hardliners are piling the pressure on Iran’s government and calling for the removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad’s resignation is also failing to ease the pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian As the war continues and diplomatic efforts to find a solution make little headway, the internal power struggle is intensifying. President Pezeshkian’s government is the focus of mounting tension Hardliners in Iran's parliament are pushing for impeachment proceedings against Araghchi. A trigger for the discontent was Araghchi's meeting with US negotiators on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

items.title: Zimbabwean author denies using AI to write award-winning story
items.summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza says he was inspired by a poem about fish tanks to write a story about his family struggles in Zimbabwe Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using artificial intelligence (AI) to write his short story, which won this year's Caine Prize for African Writing His statement comes a week after he scooped the £10,000 ($13,000) award and a recent article in The Atlantic said AI-detection software Pangram had shown his work about a boy whose family falls on hard times was entirely AI generated "For the avoidance of doubt, I wrote The Blue Fighter," he posted on X , external The accusation has caused an uproar on social media and Caine Prize chair Ellah Wakatama told the BBC she was shocked that the US magazine had not waited for a full investigation before publishing "I do wish The Atlantic had spent more time investigating this so that alongside Pangram, they did have evidence of real human investigation of it before tainting the prize and tainting this winner," Wakatama told the BBC's Front Row programme The chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees…

items.title: Germany news: Nord Stream sabotage suspect's trial opens
items.summary: A Ukrainian man is going on trial in Hamburg in the case of a 2022 attack on major gas pipelines. At the same time, Chancellor Merz is expected to give a major policy statement. DW has more Here is a roundup of all the headlines across Germany on Wednesday, October 14: Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add DW as a Preferred Source on Google The suicide rate in Germany has continued to climb, according to official statistics just released by the Federal Ministry of Health In 2025, at least 11,334 people killed themselves in Germany. That is a 9.3% increase on the previous year, and 15.6% higher than the average over the past decade This is higher than the number of deaths due to traffic accidents, AIDS, murder and manslaughter put together The data shows that this is partly due to more women (a 17.9% increase since 2021) taking their own lives, though most suicides are still carried out by men.
